get.description:
Returns a paginated list of branches for the account.

This is a v2 native-entity endpoint served from the `/v2/api/entity` base and authenticated with a Bearer token. **Requires the Branches plugin to be enabled on the account.**

The trailing path segment (`1`) is the **data level** — how deeply related records are loaded — not a page number. `/branch/list` and `/branch/list/1` return the same result. Pagination is controlled by the `page` and `per_page` query parameters.

| Parameter | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `page` | Page number (default `1`). |
| `per_page` | Items per page (default `20`). |
| `filter[<field>][<operator>]` | Filter rows by a field's value, e.g. `filter[status][equal]=1`. |
| `sort[<field>]` | Sort by a field, `asc` or `desc`, e.g. `sort[code]=asc`. |

**Filterable fields.** Filter with `filter[<field>][<operator>]=<value>`. The fields intended for filtering:

| Field | Type | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `code` | string | `filter[code][equal]=00001` |
| `status` | integer (`1`, `2`, `3`) | `filter[status][equal]=1` |

**Sorting.** Sort with `sort[<field>]=asc|desc`, e.g. `sort[code]=asc`. No field is specifically flagged for sorting; the list will in fact filter and sort on any existing column. When no `sort` is given the default ordering is newest first (`id` descending).

This API exposes six branch fields only — `id`, `name`, `status`, `created`, `modified`, and `code`. Other branch attributes (phone numbers, address, city, state, country, assigned staff, SMTP account, map location) are **not** available through this endpoint.

The `status` value is one of:

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `1` | Active |
| `2` | Inactive |
| `3` | Suspended |

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number. Defaults to `1`.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Items per page. Defaults to `20`.

parameters.name: filter[<field>][<operator>]
parameters.description: Filter rows by a field's value, e.g. `filter[status][equal]=1` or `filter[code][equal]=00001`. Filterable fields intended for use: `code`, `status` (the API also accepts any other existing column).

parameters.name: sort[<field>]
parameters.description: Sort by a field, `asc` or `desc`, e.g. `sort[code]=asc`. Default ordering is `id` descending.

parameters.description: You can generate the bearer token using the the authorization endpoint then use it here to be able to operate over your account's data

parameters.name: apikey
parameters.description: You can find/generate your apikey(s) from inside your Daftra Account

post.description:
Updates an existing branch. This posts to the same `/v2/api/entity/branch` path as create; the record to update is identified by the **`id` in the request body**. If `id` is omitted a new branch is created instead.

This is a v2 native-entity endpoint served from the `/v2/api/entity` base and authenticated with a Bearer token. **Requires the Branches plugin to be enabled on the account.**

**This is a partial merge, not a full overwrite.** Only the fields you include in the body are changed; any field you omit is left untouched. The updatable fields are `name`, `code`, and `status`. Only these fields can be updated — `id`, `name`, `status`, `created`, `modified`, and `code`. Other branch attributes (phone numbers, address, city, state, country, assigned staff, SMTP account, map location) are **not** available through this endpoint.

On success the response is `{ "message": <localized text>, "id": <id> }`. The success message is the same text returned by create, so it does not distinguish an update from an insert.

The `status` value is one of:

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `1` | Active |
| `2` | Inactive |
| `3` | Suspended |

get.description:
Returns a lightweight reference list for one whitelisted model as a flat map of `id` → `title`. Handy for populating dropdowns and lookups.

**Authentication:** this endpoint uses the `apikey` header only (send your account API key). The `Authorization: Bearer` token is not used here.

**Response shape:** `data.Listing` is a flat object whose keys are record ids and whose values are the record titles (plain strings). There is no pagination, sorting, or free-text search.

**Allowed `model` values** (case-sensitive):

| Model | Returns |
|---|---|
| `Category` | Categories, `id` → name |
| `InvoiceLayout` | Invoice layouts, `id` → name |
| `GroupPrice` | Price lists, `id` → name |
| `Role` | Staff roles, `id` → name |
| `Timezone` | Time zones, `id` → label |
| `Language` | Active languages, `id` → `Name (CODE)` |
| `Project` | Active projects, `id` → name |
| `TimeActivity` | Active time activities, `id` → name |
| `DateFormats` | Available date-format strings |

Any value outside this list returns `404 Invalid Endpoint`.

**Optional filtering** (honored only by `Category`, `InvoiceLayout`, `GroupPrice`, and `Role`; ignored by the other models):

- `fields` — an array of exactly two field names, `[keyField, valueField]`, that overrides which columns are used as the map key and value. Sending any number of elements other than two returns `400 Bad Request`.
- `conditions` — a map of `field: value` filters applied to the query.

parameters.name: model
parameters.description:
The reference model to list. Case-sensitive; must be one of the allowed values.

| Value | Returns |
|---|---|
| `Category` | Categories |
| `InvoiceLayout` | Invoice layouts |
| `GroupPrice` | Price lists |
| `Role` | Staff roles |
| `Timezone` | Time zones |
| `Language` | Active languages |
| `Project` | Active projects |
| `TimeActivity` | Active time activities |
| `DateFormats` | Available date formats |

parameters.description: You can find/generate your apikey(s) from inside your Daftra Account

Listing.description: Flat map of record id (key) to record title (value).

400.description: Returned when the `fields` query parameter is present but does not contain exactly two elements.

401.description: Returned when the `apikey` header is missing or does not match the account API key. Note the envelope differs from other errors: it carries `success` and `message` only.

404.description: Returned when `model` is not one of the allowed values (the request does not match a valid endpoint).

get.description:
Returns a paginated list of records for a workflow-type entity. This is a v2 native-entity endpoint served from the `/v2/api/entity` base and authenticated with a Bearer token.

Workflow-type entities are configurable record types (for example maintenance orders or service requests). The `workflow_id` path segment selects the workflow type, and the resource prefix plus that id form the entity key `le_workflow-type-entity-{workflow_id}`. Each record is a work-order-based row belonging to that type. The available fields — including any custom fields — are defined by the selected workflow type's configuration, so the record shape varies between workflow types; custom fields are returned under the `le_workflow-type-entity-{workflow_id}_custom_data` object.

The trailing path segment is the **data level** — how deeply related records are loaded — not a page number or a response-format extension. Pagination is controlled by the `page` and `per_page` query parameters; results can be narrowed with `filter[...]`, ordered with `sort[...]`, and trimmed with `fields`.

Filter and sort act on the record's **own columns**. The fields below are an example for a maintenance-order workflow — the exact set is workflow-specific. Custom-data fields (returned under `le_workflow-type-entity-{workflow_id}_custom_data`) are **not** filterable or sortable through this endpoint.

**Filterable fields (example).** `filter[<field>]=<value>` (exact) or `filter[<field>][<operator>]=<value>`:

| Field | Type | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `number` | string | `filter[number][like]=000` |
| `title` | string | `filter[title][like]=order` |
| `start_date` | date | `filter[start_date][greater_than_equal]=2026-01-01` |
| `client_id` | integer | `filter[client_id][equal]=5` |

(`filter[status]` is currently ineffective for this entity, and a `search` query parameter has no effect — use `filter[...]`.)

**Sorting.** Sort with `sort[<field>]=asc|desc` (e.g. `sort[number]=desc`) on the record's columns. The scalar `sort=field` / `sort=-field` form is not supported (HTTP 400), and no default order is guaranteed — always pass `sort[...]` for stable ordering.

parameters.name: workflow_id
parameters.description: The id of the workflow type whose records to list. Combined with the resource prefix this forms the entity key `le_workflow-type-entity-{workflow_id}`.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number. Defaults to `1`.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Number of records per page. Defaults to `20`.

parameters.name: filter
parameters.description: Filter on the record's own columns, as `filter[<field>]=<value>` (exact) or `filter[<field>][<operator>]=<value>` (e.g. `filter[number][like]=000`). Only records matching all filters are returned. Custom-data fields are **not** filterable through this endpoint (see the endpoint description).

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Sort by a field using the bracket form `sort[<field>]=asc|desc` (e.g. `sort[number]=desc`). The scalar form `sort=field` / `sort=-field` is not supported and returns HTTP 400. No default ordering is guaranteed — pass `sort[...]` for a stable order.

parameters.name: fields
parameters.description: Comma-separated list of fields to include in each returned record.

parameters.name: version
parameters.description: Set to `2` to return each record through the display formatter — notably file/media fields (e.g. staff photos) come back as fully-qualified URLs. The response keys are otherwise unchanged.

parameters.name: Authorization
parameters.description: You can generate the bearer token using the the authorization endpoint then use it here to be able to operate over your account's data

parameters.name: apikey
parameters.description: You can find/generate your apikey(s) from inside your Daftra Account

200.description: Paginated list of the workflow type's records.

400.description: Returned when the request cannot be processed (invalid parameter, entity not found, or the Workflow plugin is not active for the account).

401.description: The access token is missing or invalid. A permission denial (valid token, no access) instead returns `401` with an `error` field.

get.description:
Returns a single workflow-type-entity record by id. This is a v2 native-entity endpoint served from the `/v2/api/entity` base and authenticated with a Bearer token.

The `workflow_id` path segment selects the workflow type (entity key `le_workflow-type-entity-{workflow_id}`); `record_id` is the record to fetch. The successful response is a **flat object** of the record's fields — it is not wrapped in a `data` envelope. The available fields depend on the workflow type's configuration; custom fields are returned under both the `custom_data` alias and the `le_workflow-type-entity-{workflow_id}_custom_data` object.

The trailing path segment is the **data level** (how deeply related records are loaded); it is inert for a single-record fetch and is not a response-format extension.

200.description: The workflow record as a flat object (not wrapped in a data envelope).

401.description: The access token is missing or invalid. A permission denial (valid token, no access) instead returns `401` with an `error` field.

post.description:
Creates a record in a workflow-type entity. This is a v2 native-entity endpoint served from the `/v2/api/entity` base and authenticated with a Bearer token.

The `workflow_id` path segment selects the workflow type (entity key `le_workflow-type-entity-{workflow_id}`); the new record is a work-order-based row stamped with that type. The request body is a **flat object** whose keys are the workflow type's fields. The standard fields are listed below; custom fields for the workflow type are supplied under the `le_workflow-type-entity-{workflow_id}_custom_data` object.

**Required fields are defined by the selected workflow type** and enforced server-side; when a required field is missing the response is `422` with an `errors` map naming each field. For example, workflow type 1 (Maintenance Orders) requires `number.code`, `start_date`, and `budget.currency`. The record number itself is assigned by the server (submit only `number.code`).

On success the `message` is localized to the workflow type's name, e.g. `"<name> Added Successfully"`.

parameters.name: workflow_id
parameters.description: The id of the workflow type into which the record is created. Combined with the resource prefix this forms the entity key `le_workflow-type-entity-{workflow_id}`.

parameters.name: Authorization
parameters.description: You can generate the bearer token using the the authorization endpoint then use it here to be able to operate over your account's data

parameters.name: apikey
parameters.description: You can find/generate your apikey(s) from inside your Daftra Account

generated.description: leave empty, the system will assign its value

number.description: Auto-numbering fieldset. Provide `number.code` (the numbering-scheme code); the sequential number is assigned by the server, so leave `number.generated` empty. Whether this field is required depends on the workflow type's configuration.

assigned_users.description: Ids of staff assigned to this record.

budget.description: Budget as a Currency fieldset: `number` (amount) and `currency` (ISO code). Whether `budget.currency` is required depends on the workflow type's configuration.

branch_id.description: Branch id. Defaults to the request branch when omitted.

staff_id.description: the staff member who added this instance

le_workflow-type-entity-{{workflow_id}}_.description: Per-workflow custom fields for this workflow type, keyed by field name. The available custom fields are defined by the workflow type's configuration.

200.description: Record created. `message` is localized to the workflow type's name; `id` is the new record id.

400.description: The record could not be saved. Two cases: the Workflow plugin is not active for the account → `{"message":"Plugin is not installed"}`; or a save error → `{"message":"Entity not saved","error":"<detail>"}`.

e.description: Diagnostic details of the failure (present on save errors).

401.description: The access token is missing or invalid.

422.description: Validation failed. `errors` lists the fields the workflow type requires or rejects.

errors.description: Map of field name to an array of validation messages. Field names use dot notation for nested fieldsets (e.g. `number.code`, `budget.currency`).

put.description:
Updates a record in a workflow-type entity. This is a v2 native-entity endpoint served from the `/v2/api/entity` base and authenticated with a Bearer token. Both `PUT` and `POST` to this path are accepted.

The `workflow_id` path segment selects the workflow type (entity key `le_workflow-type-entity-{workflow_id}`) and `record_id` identifies the record. The request body is a **flat object** whose keys are the workflow type's fields and **must include `id` matching `record_id`**. Custom fields are supplied under the `le_workflow-type-entity-{workflow_id}_custom_data` object (include its existing row `id` to update in place).

**Required fields are defined by the selected workflow type** and enforced server-side; a missing required field returns `400` with an `errors` map (note: unlike create, which returns `422`). On success the `message` is localized to the workflow type's name, e.g. `"<name> Updated Successfully"`.

parameters.name: workflow_id
parameters.description: The id of the workflow type. Combined with the resource prefix this forms the entity key `le_workflow-type-entity-{workflow_id}`.

parameters.name: apikey
parameters.description: You can find/generate your apikey(s) from inside your Daftra Account

id.description: The id of the record to update. Must match the `record_id` in the URL.

number.description: Auto-numbering fieldset. Provide `number.code` (the numbering-scheme code) only if changing it. Required only when the workflow type requires it.

budget.description: Budget as a Currency fieldset (`number`, `currency`). Required per the workflow type's configuration.

le_workflow-type-entity-{{workflow_id}}_.description: Per-workflow custom fields to update. Include the existing custom-data row `id` to update it in place; the available fields are defined by the workflow type.

200.description: Record updated. `message` is localized to the workflow type's name; `id` is the record id.

400.description: The update could not be completed. Cases: record not found → `{"message":"Record not found"}`; validation failure → `{"message":"Entity not saved","errors":{...}}`; save error → `{"message":"Entity not saved","error":"<detail>"}`; or a permission denial → `{"message":"<reason>"}`.

errors.description: Present on validation failure: map of field name to validation messages (dot notation for nested fieldsets).

401.description: The access token is missing or invalid.

404.description: The record could not be loaded for update.

post.description:
Fetches data for **multiple entities in a single request**. The request body is a JSON **array** of sub-requests; each sub-request independently reads one entity — either a single record (`show`) or a filtered list (`list`).

`POST /v2/api/multi-entity`

The response is a **single JSON object** whose keys are each sub-request's `alias` (or its `key` when no alias is given). Each value holds that sub-request's result, so one call can return, for example, an invoice together with its related requisitions.

## Sub-request fields

| Field | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| key | Yes | The entity key to read (e.g. `invoice`, `requisition`, `follow_up_reminder`). |
| action | Yes | `show` to fetch a single record, `list` to fetch a filtered list. Any other value returns `{ "error": "Action not found" }` under that alias. |
| options | Yes | Depends on `action`. For `show`: the record **id**. For `list`: a **filters object** (see below). |
| alias | No | The key under which this sub-request's result appears in the response. Defaults to `key`. Use it to disambiguate two sub-requests that read the same entity. |
| level | No | Data-detail level — how deeply related records are loaded. Defaults to `1`. Higher levels return more nested relations. |

### `options` by action

- **`show`** — `options` is the record id, e.g. `"options": "172185"`.
- **`list`** — `options` is an object of filter conditions merged into the listing query, e.g. `"options": { "order_id": "172185", "order_type": 3 }`. Any field the target entity supports may be used.

## Response

Always returns **HTTP 200**. The body is an object keyed by each sub-request's `alias`:

- A `show` sub-request → the record object (with a `custom_data` property holding the record's custom-field values, when the entity has any).
- A `list` sub-request → a paginated envelope (`data` array plus `current_page`, `per_page`, `total`, `last_page`, and page-URL fields).
- A failed sub-request → `{ "error": "<message>" }`.

Sub-requests are processed independently: a failure in one (unknown action, inactive plugin, no permission to view the record, or an otherwise invalid sub-request) is reported as an `error` object under that alias and never fails the whole call. The overall HTTP status is always `200`.

> **Permissions:** a `show` sub-request requires permission to view the requested entity; without it that alias returns `{ "error": "You are not allowed to view this page" }`.

## Authentication

Send an OAuth Bearer access token in the `Authorization` header. Also send `Accept: application/json`.

parameters.name: Authorization
parameters.description: You can generate the bearer token using the the authorization endpoint then use it here to be able to operate over your account's data

parameters.name: apikey
parameters.description: You can find/generate your apikey(s) from inside your Daftra Account

schema.description: Array of sub-requests. Each item reads one entity, as a single record (`show`) or a filtered list (`list`).

key.description: The entity key to read, e.g. `invoice`, `requisition`, `follow_up_reminder`.

action.description:
What to fetch for this entity.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| show | Fetch a single record; `options` is the record id. |
| list | Fetch a filtered list; `options` is a filters object. |

Any other value returns `{ "error": "Action not found" }` under this sub-request's alias.

options.description:
Depends on `action`.

- **`show`** — the record id (e.g. `"172185"`).
- **`list`** — an object of filter conditions merged into the listing query (e.g. `{ "order_id": "172185", "order_type": 3 }`). Any field the target entity supports may be used.

alias.description: The key under which this sub-request's result appears in the response. Optional; defaults to `key`.

level.description: Data-detail level — how deeply related records are loaded. Optional; defaults to `1`. Higher levels return more nested relations.

schema.description: An object keyed by each sub-request's `alias` (or `key` when no alias was given). Each value is the result of one sub-request.

additionalProperties.description: Result for one sub-request — one of three shapes depending on the sub-request's `action` and whether it succeeded.

oneOf.description: `show` result — the requested record's fields, plus a `custom_data` object holding its custom-field values (present when the entity supports custom fields). The exact fields depend on the entity.

custom_data.description: The record's custom-field values, or null when it has none.

oneOf.description: `list` result — a paginated envelope of matching records.

data.description: The matching records. Fields depend on the requested entity and `level`.

from.description: Index of the first record on this page (null when empty).

next_page_url.description: URL of the next page (null on the last page).

prev_page_url.description: URL of the previous page (null on the first page).

to.description: Index of the last record on this page (null when empty).

oneOf.description: Failure for this sub-request. The other sub-requests are unaffected and the overall status stays `200`.

error.description: Human-readable reason, e.g. `Action not found`, `Plugin <name> not active`, or `You are not allowed to view this page`.

401.description:
The request has no valid OAuth Bearer access token. Send `Accept: application/json` to receive this JSON body; without it an HTML error page is returned instead.

Note: this is the only case that fails the whole request. Per-sub-request problems (unknown action, inactive plugin, no view permission) are reported inside the `200` body, not as a `401`.

message.description: Present when the request is unauthenticated (missing or invalid access token). Example: `Unauthenticated.`

get.description:
List records of any entity, addressed by its `entityKey` (e.g. `client`, `product`, `cost_center`, `work_order`).

This is a generic, metadata-driven endpoint: the columns of each returned record are defined per entity, so the field set differs by `entityKey`. Use the entity schema/fields endpoints to discover an entity's fields.

**Authentication & authorization.** Requires an OAuth2 Bearer token. The caller must hold the entity's **view** permission; otherwise the request is rejected with `401`.

**Response modes.** The `mode` query parameter selects the response shape (default `api`, a paginated list):

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| api | Paginated list (default). |
| paginate | Paginated list. |
| listing | Lightweight id/label list, for dropdowns. |
| count | Returns only `{ "total": <n> }`. |
| export | Export-oriented payload. |
| nav | Navigation (prev/next) payload. |

**Filtering.** Pass nested filters as `filter[<field>][<operator>]=<value>` (operators include `equal`, `like`); group alternatives under `filter[or][<field>][<operator>]=<value>`.

**Field selection.** Pass `fields[]=<column>` (repeatable) to limit the columns returned.

parameters.name: entityKey
parameters.description: The entity key whose records to list, e.g. `client`, `product`, `cost_center`, `work_order`.

parameters.name: dataLevel
parameters.description: Depth of related/nested data to load (higher loads more relations). Optional; defaults to `2` when omitted.

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description: Response shape. Defaults to `api` (paginated). One of `api`, `paginate`, `listing`, `count`, `export`, `nav`.

parameters.name: fields[]
parameters.description: Repeatable. Restrict the returned columns to the listed fields.

parameters.name: filter[<field>][<operator>]
parameters.description: Nested filter, e.g. `filter[business_name][like]=acme`. Operators include `equal` and `like`. Use `filter[or][...]` for OR groups.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Records per page for paginated modes.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number for paginated modes.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Sort field and direction; persisted as the caller's sorting preference for this entity.

parameters.name: version
parameters.description: When set to `2`, each row is post-formatted for display (honours `image_size`).

parameters.name: Authorization

get.description:
Fetch a single record of any entity, addressed by its `entityKey` and primary key `id`.

This is a generic, metadata-driven endpoint: the returned record's columns are defined per entity, so the field set differs by `entityKey`. The record's own columns appear at the top level and related data is nested under the relation name.

When the entity has custom fields, the matching custom-fields row is included under `custom_data`.

**Authentication & authorization.** Requires an OAuth2 Bearer token and the entity's **view** permission; otherwise the request is rejected with `401`.

parameters.description: The entity key, e.g. `client`, `product`, `cost_center`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The record's primary key.

parameters.name: dataLevel
parameters.description: Depth of related/nested data to load. Optional; defaults to `1`. A non-numeric value is treated as `1`. For single-page-app entities a suitable level is chosen automatically when omitted.

post.description:
Create a record for any entity, addressed by its `entityKey` (e.g. `client`, `cost_center`, `work_order`).

This is a generic, metadata-driven endpoint. The request body is a JSON object of the new record's field values; **which keys are accepted and which are required is defined by the entity's field metadata, so it differs per `entityKey`**. Use the entity schema/fields endpoints to discover an entity's fields and their requirements.

On success the response carries a confirmation `message` and the new record's `id`.

**Authentication & authorization.** Requires an OAuth2 Bearer token and the entity's **create** permission; otherwise the request is rejected with `401`.

get.description:
Generic, metadata-driven listing endpoint for the v2 API. It returns a **paginated, filtered, sorted** list of records for any supported entity, using a single consistent query grammar.

`GET /v2/api/entity/{entity}/list/{level}`

- **`{entity}`** — the entity key to list (e.g. `invoice`, `client`, `product`). The endpoint works for every listable entity; the enum on the `entity` path parameter is a representative sample, not the complete set.
- **`{level}`** — the *data-detail level*: how deeply related records are loaded. It is **not** a page number. Higher levels return more nested relations.

  | Level | What is returned |
  |---|---|
  | -1 | Base record fields only, no related records |
  | 0 | Own fields + one-to-one related records |
  | 1 | Own fields + one-to-one + belongs-to + one-to-many (one level deep) |
  | 2 | Same as level 1 plus one extra level of nested relations (default) |
  | 3 | Even deeper nesting |

## Pagination

Paging is controlled by the `page` and `per_page` query parameters, **not** by the URL. The response is a standard paginated envelope (`data` array + `current_page`, `per_page`, `total`, `last_page`, page-URL fields).

## Filtering

Filters use bracket syntax: `filter[<field>][<operator>]=<value>`. Combine conditions with `filter[and][...]` and `filter[or][...]` groups. See the `filter[<field>][<operator>]` parameter for the full list of operators.

## Sorting

Sort with `sort[<field>]=<direction>`, where direction is `asc` or `desc`. Multiple sort keys are applied in order, e.g. `sort[created]=desc&sort[id]=asc`.

## Field selection

Restrict the returned columns with `fields[]=<column>` (repeat for each column). When omitted, all fields for the requested level are returned.

## Authentication

Send an OAuth Bearer access token in the `Authorization` header.

parameters.name: entity
parameters.description: The entity key to list. The listed values are a representative sample — the endpoint supports every listable entity (core and custom).

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description:
Response shape / listing mode. Defaults to `api` when omitted.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| api | Paginated API response (default). Rows are reshaped so related records are nested objects. |
| listing | Paginated response used by the web UI listing (v2 formatting). |
| count | Returns only the total count of matching records. |
| export | Returns data prepared for export. |
| nav | Navigation mode; used with `current_id` to fetch neighbouring records. |

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number to return. Defaults to `1`.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Number of records per page. Defaults to `20`.

parameters.name: fields[]
parameters.description: Restrict the returned columns. Repeat for each column, e.g. `fields[]=id&fields[]=no`. When omitted, all fields for the requested level are returned.

parameters.name: sort[<field>]
parameters.description: Sort the results. Use `sort[<field>]=<direction>` where direction is `asc` or `desc`. Repeat for multiple keys; they are applied in the given order, e.g. `sort[created]=desc&sort[id]=asc`. When omitted, a saved sorting preference or the primary key is used.

parameters.name: filter[<field>][<operator>]
parameters.description:
Filter the results. Repeat the parameter for each condition.

**Syntax:** `filter[<field>][<operator>]=<value>` (omitting the operator is equivalent to `equal`).

**Operators**

| Operator | Meaning |
|---|---|
| equal | Equals (`=`) — the default when no operator is given |
| not_equal | Not equal (`!=`) |
| gt | Greater than (`>`) |
| lt | Less than (`<`) |
| gte / from | Greater than or equal (`>=`) |
| lte / to | Less than or equal (`<=`) |
| like | Contains (`LIKE %value%`) |
| in | In a list of values |
| not_in | Not in a list of values |
| is_null | Field is null |
| is_not_null | Field is not null |

Only the operators above are recognized; any other keyword is treated as `equal`. Express a range with two conditions (`filter[amount][from]=10&filter[amount][to]=99`); there is no `between` operator.

**AND / OR groups**

Wrap conditions in `filter[and][...]` or `filter[or][...]` to group them. The OR group is the usual way to run a keyword search across several fields, e.g. `filter[or][no][like]=INV&filter[or][client_business_name][like]=INV`.

parameters.name: version
parameters.description: Set to `2` to return records formatted with the v2 field formatters.

parameters.name: image_size
parameters.description: Requested image size for record images. Only applies when `version=2`.

parameters.name: request_branch_id
parameters.description: Scope the results to a specific branch by its ID.

parameters.name: lang
parameters.description: Response language. Accepts `ar` or `en`. The `Accept-Language` header is also honoured.

parameters.name: Authorization
parameters.description: You can generate the bearer token using the the authorization endpoint then use it here to be able to operate over your account's data

parameters.description: You can find/generate your apikey(s) from inside your Daftra Account

get.description:
Activates or deactivates a marketplace app for the current site.

Send `true` in the `status` path segment to activate the app, or any other value to deactivate it. When the app is not yet installed for the site, it is first installed in a deactivated state and then the requested action is applied.

The response body carries a numeric `code` describing the outcome:

| `code` | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | Error — app not found |
| 1 | App activated |
| 2 | Settings required — the app must be configured before it can be activated |
| 3 | App deactivated |
| 4 | Payment required — the app has not been purchased or renewed |

Successful activation/deactivation and the not-found case return HTTP `200`; the *settings required* (`2`) and *payment required* (`4`) cases return HTTP `400`. Branch on `status`/`code`, not only on the HTTP status.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The marketplace app id (the `id` of the app in the apps catalogue) to activate or deactivate.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Whether to activate or deactivate the app. Send `true` to activate; any other value deactivates.

parameters.name: Authorization
parameters.description: You can generate the bearer token using the the authorization endpoint then use it here to be able to operate over your account's data

parameters.name: apikey
parameters.description: You can find/generate your apikey(s) from inside your Daftra Account

200.description:
Activation/deactivation outcome. Example bodies:

Activated:
```json
{ "status": true, "code": 1, "msg": "App activated successfully" }
```
Deactivated:
```json
{ "status": true, "code": 3, "msg": "App deactivated successfully" }
```
App not found (still HTTP 200):
```json
{ "status": false, "code": 0, "msg": "App not found" }
```

schema.description: The activation/deactivation outcome. Successful activation, successful deactivation, and the not-found case all return HTTP `200` — inspect `status`/`code` to distinguish them.

status.description: `true` when the requested activation or deactivation succeeded; `false` when the app id was not found.

code.description:
Outcome code. For HTTP `200` responses this is one of:

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 1 | App activated |
| 3 | App deactivated |
| 0 | App not found |

msg.description: Localized, human-readable outcome message (e.g. `App activated successfully`, `App deactivated successfully`, `App not found`).

400.description:
Activation blocked. Example bodies:

Settings required:
```json
{ "status": false, "code": 2, "msg": "Settings Required" }
```
Payment required:
```json
{ "status": false, "code": 4, "msg": "You cannot activate this application because it has not been purchased or renewed. Please complete the purchase first." }
```

schema.description: The app cannot be activated yet. Returned when the app still requires configuration, or has not been purchased/renewed.

code.description:
Reason code:

| Value | Meaning |

| 2 | Settings required — the app must be configured before it can be activated |
| 4 | Payment required — the app has not been purchased or renewed |

get.description:
Locks or unlocks an entity record on behalf of an installed app.

Intended for third-party app integrations: an installed app can lock a specific record of any entity it has access to (preventing further edits) or unlock it again. Send `true` in the `lock` path segment to lock the record; any other value unlocks it.

Authenticated with an OAuth bearer token. The response is always HTTP `200` with a `{ status, msg }` object — inspect `status` to tell success from the two failure cases (the app is not installed/active for the site, or the record was not found).

parameters.name: appId
parameters.description: The installed app's id (the app performing the lock/unlock).

parameters.name: entityKey
parameters.description: The entity key of the record to lock/unlock (e.g. `product`, `invoice`).

parameters.name: entityId
parameters.description: The id of the record within the entity.

parameters.name: lock
parameters.description: Send `true` to lock the record; any other value unlocks it.

parameters.name: Authorization
parameters.description: You can generate the bearer token using the the authorization endpoint then use it here to be able to operate over your account's data

parameters.name: apikey
parameters.description: You can find/generate your apikey(s) from inside your Daftra Account

200.description:
Lock/unlock outcome. Example bodies:

Locked:
```json
{ "status": true, "msg": "Record locked successfully" }
```
Unlocked:
```json
{ "status": true, "msg": "Record unlocked successfully" }
```
App not installed/inactive (still HTTP 200):
```json
{ "status": false, "msg": "App is not installed or inactive" }
```
Record not found (still HTTP 200):
```json
{ "status": false, "msg": "Record not found" }
```

schema.description: The lock/unlock outcome. Always returned with HTTP `200` — inspect `status` to distinguish success from the two failure cases.

status.description: `true` when the record was locked/unlocked; `false` when the app is not installed/active for the site, or the record was not found.

msg.description:
Localized, human-readable outcome message.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Record locked successfully | The record is now locked. |
| Record unlocked successfully | The record is now unlocked. |
| App is not installed or inactive | The app is not installed or not active for the current site. |
| Record not found | No record matches the given entity/id. |

schema.description: Authentication failed or was missing (a valid OAuth bearer token is required).

message.description: Returned when no valid access token is supplied.

get.description:
Returns the activation status of a marketplace app for the current site.

An app is reported active only when it is **installed and active** for the authenticated site. The response is always HTTP `200` with a `{ status, msg }` object — including when the app id does not exist, in which case `status` is `false` and `msg` is `App not found`. Use the `status` boolean (not the HTTP code) to branch.

| `status` | `msg` | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `true` | App is active | The app is installed and active for the current site. |
| `false` | App is deactivated | The app exists but is not active for the current site. |
| `false` | App not found | No app matches the given id (or the app is unavailable). |

The `msg` text is localized to the account language.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The marketplace app id (the `id` of the app in the apps catalogue) whose activation status you want to check.

parameters.name: Authorization
parameters.description: You can generate the bearer token using the the authorization endpoint then use it here to be able to operate over your account's data

parameters.name: apikey
parameters.description: You can find/generate your apikey(s) from inside your Daftra Account

200.description:
Activation status of the app for the current site. Example bodies:

Active:
```json
{ "status": true, "msg": "App is active" }
```
Deactivated:
```json
{ "status": false, "msg": "App is deactivated" }
```
Not found (still HTTP 200):
```json
{ "status": false, "msg": "App not found" }
```

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| App is active | Installed and active for the current site. |
| App is deactivated | Exists but not active for the current site. |
| App not found | No app matches the id (or the app is unavailable). |
